summary:
A.U.R.O.R.A. is an interactive Earth observation and environmental intelligence platform developed to address the NASA Space Apps Challenge “Be An Earth System Trend Detective!”

Our solution transforms 25 years of NASA satellite observations into interactive maps, statistical analyses, and AI-powered predictions. It integrates seven primary datasets, 2,097 monthly maps, and over 85.9 million valid satellite-derived values across Querétaro, Mexico, and the world.

Users can investigate vegetation health, land surface temperature, precipitation, environmental anomalies, and statistically significant trends. Four evaluated machine learning models provide predictive capabilities for Querétaro.

By combining Earth science, data engineering, artificial intelligence, and accessible visualization, A.U.R.O.R.A. empowers students, researchers, and communities to explore environmental changes and make informed, evidence-based decisions.

Our mission is to make Earth observation accessible, understandable, and reproducible.
details:
A.U.R.O.R.A. — Exploring Earth. Understanding Change.

The problem

Earth is constantly changing. However, accessing, processing, and interpreting decades of satellite observations requires specialized knowledge, computational resources, and technical expertise.

A.U.R.O.R.A. bridges this gap through an integrated environmental intelligence platform.

Our solution

We developed a bilingual desktop application that transforms NASA satellite observations into interactive scientific experiences, combining data engineering, geospatial analysis, statistics, and artificial intelligence.

Scientific scope

  • 7 primary satellite datasets.
  • 2,097 monthly environmental maps.
  • 85,940,785 valid satellite-derived cell-month-variable values.
  • 3 geographical scales: Querétaro, Mexico, and global.
  • 3 environmental variables: NDVI, land surface temperature (LST), and precipitation.
  • 12 scientific result packages.
  • 4 evaluated machine learning models.
  • 166 successfully passed automated tests.

NDVI and LST observations cover January 2001 through December 2025. Global precipitation observations extend through September 2025.

Platform capabilities

  • Mission Control: centralized environmental information.
  • Planetary Explorer: interactive geographical visualization.
  • Time Machine: historical environmental exploration.
  • Statistical Laboratory: trend detection and significance testing.
  • Multivariate Laboratory: correlations, anomalies, and relationships between environmental variables.
  • Predictive Intelligence: XGBoost and ConvLSTM models for Querétaro.

Scientific methodology

Our pipeline acquires NASA MODIS and GPM observations through Google Earth Engine, applies quality controls, harmonizes geographical grids, and organizes observations into efficient multidimensional datasets using NPZ and Zarr.

The scientific engine incorporates ordinary least squares, Sen's slope, autocorrelation-aware statistical inference, false discovery rate correction, Pearson and Spearman correlations, seasonal anomalies, and temporal lag analysis.

Missing observations are not presented as measured values. Correlation is not interpreted as causation.

Artificial intelligence

Four trained models were evaluated using held-out historical observations from 2022–2025.

NDVI:

  • XGBoost: R² = 0.8844.
  • ConvLSTM: R² = 0.8841.

Land surface temperature:

  • XGBoost: R² = 0.8194.
  • ConvLSTM: R² = 0.7955.

Predictive capabilities are currently qualified for Querétaro. Predictions remain clearly distinguishable from satellite observations.

Technology and reproducibility

A.U.R.O.R.A. was developed using Python, Google Earth Engine, NumPy, SciPy, Pandas, Rasterio, Zarr, Statsmodels, XGBoost, PyTorch, PySide6, and Matplotlib.

Two portable release candidates were generated:

  • AURORA Full: approximately 718 MiB.
  • AURORA Lite: approximately 92 MiB.

Both editions passed SHA-256 integrity checks and inference validation in a CPU-only Linux environment. Windows installation recipes are provided but have not yet been functionally validated.

Intended impact

A.U.R.O.R.A. aims to democratize Earth observation, support environmental education, facilitate scientific exploration, and encourage evidence-based decision-making.

AI assistance disclosure

OpenAI ChatGPT and Codex assisted with software development, code generation, debugging, technical planning, documentation, and submission text. Satellite observations originate from the cited NASA datasets; they were not generated by generative AI.

A.U.R.O.R.A. transforms decades of Earth observations into opportunities for discovery.

Explore the Earth. Understand its changes.
